# Informatico.ai

> 48 interactive long-form essays on civil engineering, architecture, physics and mathematics, in English and Spanish, each with a live model to explore.

Every essay, bounty folio, and 3D CAD toolbox folio is also in Mexican Spanish under https://informatico.ai/es-mx/. Public open-source repository (60 SKILL.md companions, Python verifiers, 6 Bounty Crucible harnesses & 6 Tech & Tools 3D CAD generators): https://github.com/senseiewok/informatico.ai . For learning and research, not professional or medical advice.

## Civil Engineering & Construction

- [Civil Engineering & Construction](https://informatico.ai/engineering/): Twelve interactive essays on civil engineering and construction: concrete pumping, 3D printing, bridges, tunnel boring machines and self-healing concrete.
- [E.01 Stokes–Brinkman Flow in Porous Materials](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e01/): How viscous shear and Darcy drag balance inside porous limestone, capillary mortars and biological hydrogels, with an interactive percolation model.
- [E.02 Herschel–Bulkley Rheology of Pumped Concrete](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e02/): How the yield-stress rheology of Bingham, Herschel and Bulkley sets pipe pressure, forms a solid plug core and keeps concrete pumping free of blockages.
- [E.03 Acoustic Metamaterials: Helmholtz Sound Absorbers](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e03/): How coiled quarter-wave resonators and micro-slit boundary layers absorb nearly all low-frequency sound in a panel 1/19th of a wavelength thick.
- [E.04 Counter-Current Enthalpy Recovery Exchangers](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e04/): How membrane exchangers pass heat and water vapor from exhaust to supply air, recovering 88.2% sensible and 79.4% latent energy without frost.
- [E.05 Terzaghi Soil Mechanics and CFA Deep Foundations](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e05/): How Karl Terzaghi's effective stress principle and consolidation theory, with continuous flight auger piles, govern building settlement and liquefaction.
- [E.06 Nonlinear Structural Dynamics and Seismic Isolation](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e06/): How Biot's earthquake spectra, Newmark–Hall ductility and Robinson's lead-rubber bearings decouple hospitals and laboratories from ground motion.
- [E.07 Suspension Bridge Flutter and Scanlan Derivatives](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e07/): How Robert Scanlan's flutter derivatives govern twin-box bridge decks in extreme wind, and how physics-informed neural networks read them from few sensors.
- [E.08 EPB Tunnel Boring Machines and Settlement Troughs](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e08/): How the Peck–Mair Gaussian settlement trough predicts ground movement above city tunnels, paired with graph neural network twins of the subsurface.
- [E.09 Self-Healing Concrete: Bacterial and Crystalline](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e09/): How Bacillus pseudofirmus spores and crystalline admixtures seal microcracks in concrete by growing calcium carbonate, tracked with ultrasonic coda waves.
- [E.10 3D Concrete Printing: Extrusion and Buildability](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e10/): How Nicolas Roussel's thixotropic structuration and Suiker's buckling laws decide whether a robot-printed concrete wall stands without formwork.
- [E.11 SIMP Topology Optimization and Inerter Damping](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e11/): How Bendsøe and Sigmund's bone-like topology optimization and Formula 1 flywheel inerters cut floor concrete by 65% while calming wind sway in towers.
- [E.12 Verified RISC-V Silicon and Firefly Grid Control](https://informatico.ai/engineering/e12/): How Anthropic's 180-million-line Rocq proof for RISC-V chips, Control Barrier Functions and firefly phase-locking stabilize renewable power grids.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://informatico.ai/architecture/): Twelve interactive essays on architecture: stone vaults, timber gridshells, Barragán's color, sky-cooling roofs and facades that move with humidity and sun.
- [A.01 Funicular Thrust Surfaces in Stone and Timber Shells](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a01/): How compression-only stone vaults and cross-laminated timber shells stand under Heyman's middle-third rule, with a condensation-free springer detail.
- [A.02 Reciprocal Timber Gridshells (Nexorades)](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a02/): How bolt-free reciprocal timber frames, where each beam rests on its neighbor, turn shell thrust into local bending and span large roofs with short pieces.
- [A.03 Double-Skin Facades and Buoyancy Stack Ventilation](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a03/): How the thermosiphon stack effect and solar shading inside multi-story ventilated glass cavities cut mechanical cooling loads without overheating.
- [A.04 From Archigram to British High-Tech Architecture](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a04/): How Archigram's 1960s Plug-In City manifestos shaped Rogers, Piano, Rice and Foster: cast-steel exoskeletons, open floors and crane-replaceable modules.
- [A.05 Room Acoustics: Sabine–Eyring Reverberation](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a05/): How Wallace Sabine's decay law, Carl Eyring's absorption formula and Manfred Schroeder's prime-sequence coffers shape reverberation and noise fatigue.
- [A.06 Net-Zero Water and Greywater Constructed Wetlands](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a06/): How Kadlec–Knight reed beds recycle 95% of building greywater, while 60 °C hot-water loops and UV-C reactors keep Legionella and Pseudomonas out.
- [A.07 Luis Barragán's Chromatic Tectonics](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a07/): How Luis Barragán, Chucho Reyes Ferreira and Josef Albers turned mineral pigments like Rosa Mexicano and Mexican sunlight into architecture of color.
- [A.08 Radiative Sky-Cooling Roofs and Phase-Change Walls](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a08/): How photonic roofs send building heat through the 8–13 μm atmospheric window into cold space, even under midday sun, paired with phase-change walls.
- [A.09 Hygroscopic Programmable Timber Skins](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a09/): How Timoshenko's bilayer curvature theory and Achim Menges's beech skins let building facades open and close with humidity, using no motors at all.
- [A.10 Miura-Ori Origami Deployable Facades](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a10/): How Koryo Miura's fold and the folded metamaterials of Schenk and Guest drive adaptive, deployable solar facades inspired by the mashrabiya screen.
- [A.11 3D Polyhedral Graphic Statics and Stone Vaults](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a11/): How James Clerk Maxwell's reciprocal force polyhedra and open-source COMPAS software design thin, unreinforced vaulted floors with 72% less concrete.
- [A.12 Tensegrity Cable Domes and Sky-Cooling Canopies](https://informatico.ai/architecture/a12/): How Sergio Pellegrino's prestressed tensegrity domes and 8–13 μm radiative sky-cooling membranes shade and cool civic plazas using zero electricity.

## Physics

- [Physics](https://informatico.ai/physics/): Twelve interactive essays on physics: Formula 1 aerodynamics, the wave physics of color, cilia and mucus, Taylor-cone aerosols and topological photonics.
- [P.01 Fluctuation–Dissipation and Allosteric Gating Energy](https://informatico.ai/physics/p01/): How Keizer's fluctuation theory, Harada–Sasa dissipation and Hill cycle diagrams measure the energy efficiency of ABC-transporter gating cycles.
- [P.02 Active Matter: Ciliary Metachronal Waves](https://informatico.ai/physics/p02/): How low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics and Kuramoto phase-lag synchronization make carpets of airway cilia beat in waves that move fluid together.
- [P.03 Mucin Hydrogel Rheology and Anomalous Subdiffusion](https://informatico.ai/physics/p03/): How Carreau–Yasuda shear-thinning, reptation and anomalous subdiffusion decide how fast gene-delivery nanoparticles can cross the airway mucus mesh.
- [P.04 Electrokinetics of Airway Surface Hydration](https://informatico.ai/physics/p04/): How Nernst–Planck electrodiffusion, Donnan swelling pressure and liquid flux across the epithelium set the critical hydration threshold of airway surfaces.
- [P.05 Quantum Tunneling: WKB Barrier Penetration](https://informatico.ai/physics/p05/): How Gamow's WKB tunneling integral, Marcus reorganization energy and kinetic isotope effects shape the chemistry of base editing of nonsense mutations.
- [P.06 de Gennes Polymer Reptation in Entangled Gels](https://informatico.ai/physics/p06/): How Pierre-Gilles de Gennes's tube model and Doi–Edwards relaxation govern how 4.5 kb mRNA and gene-editing polyplexes slither through entangled gels.
- [P.07 Formula 1 Ground-Effect Venturi Aerodynamics](https://informatico.ai/physics/p07/): How underfloor Venturi tunnels, edge vortices and the 2026 FIA active aerodynamics rules balance downforce against porpoising in Formula 1 cars.
- [P.08 The Wave Physics of Color](https://informatico.ai/physics/p08/): How light waves between 380 and 780 nm make pearlescent car paint shift color with angle, while Luis Barragán's lime walls keep a calm, steady hue.
- [P.09 Electrohydrodynamic Taylor Cones and Aerosols](https://informatico.ai/physics/p09/): How Sir Geoffrey Taylor's 49.3° equilibrium cone and the Rayleigh charge limit govern electrospray, a precise way to turn a liquid into a fine aerosol.
- [P.10 Topological Photonics and Chern Numbers](https://informatico.ai/physics/p10/): How Haldane and Raghu's Berry curvature and integer Chern numbers let light and sound flow around sharp defects with zero reflection.
- [P.11 Surface-Code Quantum Computing and Clean Nitrogen](https://informatico.ai/physics/p11/): How Kitaev's topological surface-code stabilizers in Stim and PySCF quantum phase estimation decode room-temperature nitrogen fertilizer catalysis.
- [P.12 Hilbert's Sixth Problem: Atoms to Navier–Stokes](https://informatico.ai/physics/p12/): How Yu Deng, Zaher Hani and Xiao Ma derived the incompressible Navier–Stokes fluid equations from colliding Newtonian spheres over long times.

## Mathematics

- [Mathematics](https://informatico.ai/math/): Twelve interactive essays on mathematics: Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean 4, F1 optimal control, the geometry of color, optimal transport and topology.
- [M.01 Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean 4: Modularity Lifting](https://informatico.ai/math/m01/): How the Lean 4 formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem and Taylor–Wiles patching work, and how their stepwise proofs mirror energy landscapes.
- [M.02 Riemann Zeta Zero-Density Estimates in Lean 4](https://informatico.ai/math/m02/): Inside the Zeta23 and XiPrime Lean 4 proofs: how mathematicians bound exceptions to the Riemann critical line and what spectral gaps describe.
- [M.03 Cap Sets, FunSearch and AlphaEvolve](https://informatico.ai/math/m03/): How Google DeepMind's FunSearch found larger cap sets and AlphaEvolve multiplied 4×4 complex matrices with 48 products, reshaping extremal combinatorics.
- [M.04 Polynomial Freiman–Ruzsa and the Magma Graph](https://informatico.ai/math/m04/): How Terence Tao and the Lean community formalized Marton's conjecture with entropy methods and mapped all 4,694 × 4,694 pairs of magma laws.
- [M.05 AlphaGeometry 2: Neuro-Symbolic Deductive Search](https://informatico.ai/math/m05/): How pairing a symbolic deduction engine with neural auxiliary-point generation solves Olympiad geometry, and how the same idea locates 3D binding sites.
- [M.06 Fine-Grained Complexity and Process Supervision](https://informatico.ai/math/m06/): How Ryan Williams's APSP speedup and step-level process reward models prune errors in formal proof search and in genomic off-target scans.
- [M.07 F1 Energy Control with Pontryagin's Maximum Principle](https://informatico.ai/math/m07/): How Pontryagin's Maximum Principle schedules the 350 kW electric boost of 2026 Formula 1 cars without clipping the battery, sped up by neural operators.
- [M.08 The Riemannian Geometry of Color Perception](https://informatico.ai/math/m08/): How Grassmann's projection creates metamers, colors that look the same but differ in light, and how Schrödinger's curved metric defines true hue paths.
- [M.09 Monge–Kantorovich Optimal Transport](https://informatico.ai/math/m09/): How Jean-David Benamou and Yann Brenier showed that Wasserstein-2 optimal transport is a fluid flow along geodesics, governed by Hamilton–Jacobi.
- [M.10 Persistent Homology and Percolating Pores](https://informatico.ai/math/m10/): How Edelsbrunner, Letscher and Zomorodian's persistent homology finds the pore throats that let fluid percolate through materials at every scale.
- [M.11 The 3D Kakeya Conjecture and Riemann Zero Bounds](https://informatico.ai/math/m11/): How Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl solved the 3D Kakeya needle conjecture, paired with Guth and Maynard's 30/13 Riemann zero-density breakthrough.
- [M.12 Anthropic Lean 4 Complexity and Post-Quantum Locks](https://informatico.ai/math/m12/): How Anthropic's machine-checked Lean 4 complexity proofs pair with NIST FIPS 203 crystal lattices to protect digital trust against quantum attacks.

## Open-Bounty & Prize Crucible (B.01–B.06)

- [Open-Bounty & Prize Crucible](https://informatico.ai/bounties/): Six interactive bounty folios with reproducible Python verifiers and AI skills for Erdős Lean 4 problems, XPRIZE Quantum, Carbon Removal and Sky-Cooling.
- [B.01 (BOUNTY-M1) Erdős Sidon Sets and Lean 4 Formalization Bounties](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b01/): How Mian–Chowla greedy sequences, the Erdős–Turán upper bound and Lean 4 formal proofs test Sidon sets, with a reproducible Python verifier.
- [B.02 (BOUNTY-P1) XPRIZE Quantum and Surface-Code FeMoCo Catalysis](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b02/): How Kitaev's topological surface-code stabilizers in Stim and PySCF quantum phase estimation bound the physical qubits for nitrogen fixation.
- [B.03 (BOUNTY-E1) XPRIZE Carbon Removal: SIMP Mineralized Floor Slabs](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b03/): How Bendsøe–Sigmund SIMP topology optimization in FEniCS and carbonate mineralization cut floor slab embodied carbon below 45 kg per square meter.
- [B.04 (BOUNTY-A1) Holcim & Cooling Prizes: 3D Vaults and Sky-Cooling](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b04/): How Maxwell 3D polyhedral graphic statics in COMPAS and 8–13 μm radiative sky-cooling roofs build zero-rebar vaults that cool below ambient air.
- [B.05 (BOUNTY-P2) PySR Symbolic Regression and PySINDy PDE Discovery](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b05/): How PySINDy sparse operator thresholding, Dedalus spectral solvers and PySR Pareto symbolic regression recover exact fluid laws from noisy sensors.
- [B.06 (BOUNTY-M2) PhysLean Gauge Anomaly & ITensors.jl Entanglement](https://informatico.ai/bounties/b06/): How HEPLean/PhysLean certifies Standard Model gauge anomaly cancellation in Lean 4 while ITensors.jl and NetKet bound critical quantum entanglement.

## Tech & Tools · The 3D CAD, Open BIM & Small-Studio Toolbox (X.01–X.06)

- [Tech & Tools · The Toolbox](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/): Six interactive 3D CAD and open-tool folios with downloadable STEP, 3MF, GLB and DXF files, Python byte-level verifiers, and skills for small studios.
- [X.01 (TOOL-CORE-1) Zero-Build WebGL2 GLB Viewer and Manifold Validator](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x01/): How a zero-dependency WebGL2 loader parses binary glTF 2.0 files while a Python stdlib verifier checks watertight topology and signed mesh volume.
- [X.02 (TOOL-ENG-1) Code-First Parametric Solids: STEP, 3MF and GLB](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x02/): How independent engineers generate parametric B-rep solids in Python and audit what survives across STEP AP242, 3MF and GLB with chordal tolerances.
- [X.03 (TOOL-ARCH-1) Small Architect's Vault, Timber and Open BIM Kit](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x03/): How small architecture studios generate compression-only stone and timber voussoir arches in Python and export verified STEP, 3MF, DXF and GLB files.
- [X.04 (TOOL-ARCH-2) Miura-Ori Kinetic Screens: 3D GLB to Laser-Cut DXF](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x04/): How small studios and makers generate deployable Miura-ori facade shells in 3D GLB and 3MF alongside layered 2D laser-cutter DXF crease patterns.
- [X.05 (TOOL-FAB-1) SIMP Structural Lattices to Watertight 3MF Meshes](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x05/): How variable-taper SIMP structural struts are synthesized as watertight 2-manifold 3MF, GLB and STEP meshes with frustum volume and overhang checks.
- [X.06 (TOOL-PHYS-MATH-1) Topological Metamaterial Cells and Betti Verifier](https://informatico.ai/toolchain/x06/): How pierced genus-one acoustic metamaterial unit cells are exported to GLB, 3MF and STEP while a Python verifier checks Euler and Betti invariants.

## Time & Gravity · Thirteen Pages on an Open Problem (T.00–T.12)

- [Time & Gravity](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/): A reading track from the measured slope in the rate of time to the open problem of time in quantum gravity, with instruments, verifiers and a ledger.
- [T.01 Gravity as a Slope in the Rate of Time](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t01/): How measured clock-rate differences between heights make a slow body fall at g with no force term, with a live geodesic instrument and a Python verifier.
- [T.02 Everyone Moves at One Rate: Clocks, GPS and c](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t02/): How moving clocks tick slower by the Lorentz factor, measured from 1938 to 2014, and how the GPS clock correction follows from GM, the orbit radius and c.
- [T.03 What Sets the Slope: Poisson and Equivalence](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t03/): How the weak-field Einstein equation reduces to Poisson's equation, and how torsion balances, lunar ranging and a satellite show every composition falls alike.
- [T.04 A Clock in Two Places: the Clock Interferometer](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t04/): An experiment description: a clock in superposition of two heights loses interference visibility as its proper times decohere, with the formula recomputed live.
- [T.05 Does Gravity Entangle? Three Channels, One Question](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t05/): Bose-Marletto-Vedral recomputed: the entanglement phase of two masses, a classical channel that entangles nothing, and the 2025 dispute, at equal weight.
- [T.06 Does Gravity Collapse the Wave? The Bound](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t06/): The Diosi-Penrose collapse proposal, its predicted spontaneous radiation, and the Gran Sasso and XENONnT bounds recomputed from the published counts.
- [T.07 The Equation with No Time: a Page-Wootters Toy](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t07/): How a stationary quantum state with a clock inside recovers Schrodinger evolution when conditioned on the clock, checked with a pure-Python eigensolver.
- [T.08 A Horizon Has a Temperature: Rindler Wedges and Hawking's Quarter](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t08/): How tracing over modes behind a causal horizon turns a pure vacuum state into a Planck thermal bath and fixes black-hole entropy at A/4.
- [T.09 A Horizon Rings Like a Bell: Kerr Quasinormal Modes and Leaver's Continued Fractions](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t09/): How a spinning Kerr black hole rings down at frequencies fixed by mass and spin alone, solved from Leaver's continued fractions and checked against GW150914 and GW250114.
- [T.10 Page's Counting Argument: the Curve on Ten Qubits](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t10/): Hawking's rising entropy against Page's curve, built from random states on ten qubits and checked against Page's formula, with the area theorem's two tests.
- [T.11 What Selects the World a Clock Sees? Einselection and Quantum Darwinism](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t11/): How pointer-commuting photon scattering suppresses spatial superpositions and broadcasts redundant classical records in the electromagnetic bath.
- [T.12 Two Clocks That Only Meet in Gravity: Dark Sectors and Clock Networks](https://informatico.ai/timegravity/t12/): How universal metric coupling lets spatially separated clocks sense electromagnetically transparent matter while co-located optical clocks bound scalar portals.

- [About Informatico & the Verification Engine](https://informatico.ai/about/): How an independent open-source lab builds interactive engineering essays, why every claim carries a verifier, and how testing these models helps research.
